about: Routing-flow features (user decision 2026-10-09: each idea from hardware-design/reports/2026-10-08-tracemaker-ideas.md is a switch here, benchmarked with and without: hardware-design/reports/2026-10-09-route-features-benchmark.md). Read by tools/route_features.py for iotroute fastroute, tools/stitch_all.ts and tools/placer/compact_cli.py. A board overrides any key in its gate.json under "route_features" (same shape, merged per feature). The environment overrides last: ROUTE_FEATURES="name=1,name=0" (all=0 / all=1 for every flag); ROUTE_BOARD=<BOARD> names the board when the PCB is a copy outside hardware-design/boards/. Defaults: see the benchmark report verdict.

triage_opens.about: After routing: each open signal connection is ENCLOSED (no legal path: flood fill over the clearance grid of the routed board) or ROUTER_MISS, with the blocking nets and parts. OUTDIR/open-triage.json and <board>/.gate/open-triage.json; one TRIAGE line.

rule_compiler.about: Before routing: the board .kicad_dru (disallow track per layer, disallow via, class-to-class clearance) and the extra rules below become Fastroute constraints: per-net layer masks and via bans (DSN class circuit use_layer: a via-banned net gets one outer layer, so no via is possible), class_class clearances. Rule areas with no tracks / no vias are already exported by KiCad as wire_keepout / via_keepout.

via_off_small_pads.about: Before routing: a DSN via_keepout over each SMD pad whose smaller side is below max_pad_mm (exposed pads and large pads keep their in-pad vias). The viapads gate still checks the result.

pin_escape_check.about: Before routing: pins that cannot leave their package (flood fill on the pad layer at the minimum track width and the net clearance: out of the footprint box, or to a place where a via fits). OUTDIR/pin-escape.json; one ESCAPE line. tools/placer/compact_cli.py adds halo_hint_mm to the spacing of those parts for the next search step.

via_halo.about: Fastroute routes the vias of the selected nets with a larger padstack (size_mm), so a ground stitching via (kicad-happy RP-001) fits beside each one; after the import the vias get their class size again. Nets: the globs in nets, the net classes in classes, the fast list of <board>/<fast_nets_file>, and the nets tools/stitch_all.ts found with no room (<board>/.gate/halo-nets.json). Generalises the CELLULAR halo (tools/cell_route.py --halo).

routing_rules.about: D-125 (user rules 2026-10-10), in iotroute fastroute. 1: staged order, each stage's copper locked for the next: pairs_clocks (diff-pairs.json, clock_patterns), fast (rp001-fast-nets.json), wide (current-paths.json, net classes wider than Default, reference-planes power patterns; a switch node in the fast list is wide), rest, then a last pass with no keepout for the plane nets (--route-planes) and the nets a stage left open (their stage copper ripped up first), then at most repair_iterations rip-up-and-repair passes (W9): the nets still open and their immediate blockers (copper within repair_corridor_mm of the open connection's straight line, the nearest repair_max_blockers nets; plane nets and grounds never) are unlocked, every other net stays locked (pair, clock and fast copper included unless it is such a blocker), signal nets with the keepouts; an iteration that leaves the same nets open ends the loop. OFF: the A/B of 2026-10-10 (D-125) lost completion. A stage is split into its signal nets (keepouts) and its power/ground/exempt nets (no keepout): Fastroute 0.1.7 has no per-net keepout. 2: --router.scoring.via_costs=via_costs unless the caller sets it; OUTDIR/via-report.json (vias per stage and net class; fast-net vias with no ground via within the spec via_allow_mm), line VIAS_BY_STAGE. 3: before each signal stage the zones are refilled and every area of a job layer whose reference-planes.json adjacent layer has no ground / alt_ref copper (keepout_grid_mm scan; a disc of pad/via radius + disc_margin_mm, at most via_allow_mm, round each pad and via of a non-reference net stays open: pin access and antipads) becomes a DSN wire_keepout. OUTDIR/stage-plan.json; lines STAGES and STAGE. Off for BASE-PWR-B (its mandatory preflight).
routing_rules.fine_pitch_source: IPC-7351B (land pattern standard): fine-pitch components have a lead pitch of 0.65 mm or less. W10 (2026-10-10): the SMD pads of each footprint whose pad pitch (smallest pad-centre distance) is at most this get the escape stage before the wide stage (the BGA fan-out practice): Fastroute --router.fanout.enabled=true over those nets only, with wire and via keepouts outside a belt round each such courtyard (one Default clearance + two staggered rows of Default vias + a Default track with its clearance); at most escape_max_time_s router seconds; the far connections fail inside the belt by design and the nets are routed again in their own stage from the locked escapes. OUTDIR/stage-plan.json escape, lines ESCAPE.
routing_rules.hot_loop_source: TI SLVAES4 and the hot-loop layout guidance: the switch node is a minimum-area loop, 'as short and direct as possible'. W10: a switch node (current-paths.json net with "switch_node": true, or a name in switch_nodes; a per-board gate.json override) is routed in its own wide_hot stage with a corridor keepout round its pads (the pad box grown by (max - straight) / 2), a use_layer mask to its SMD pads' layer (no via possible), via cost via_costs x hot_loop_via_factor, and the bound max_mm = hot_loop_factor x the straight distance of its two loop pads (1.5: no scope-board regulator datasheet gives a figure; AP63203 and the PWR-24V regulator say short and wide). The result is checked after routing: OUTDIR/via-report.json hot_loops, line VIAS_BY_STAGE ... HOT_LOOPS.

fail_fast.about: D-126 (user direction 2026-10-11, W12): fail fast in the routing step. (1) optimizer_if_routed: a caller's --optimizer always becomes if-routed: the optimizer runs only when the router pass ends with 0 routable open connections (iotroute fastroute --optimizer if-routed); with opens the job imports the router's best board, writes the triage and the UNROUTED line, prints STUCK and exits with code 3 (stuck_exit; tools/placer/compact_cli.py reads the UNROUTED line of such a step). (2) stall_passes: the router is stopped (SIGTERM: Fastroute writes its best board and the report, rc 0) when this many consecutive autorouter passes do not lower the open count below the best so far; OUTDIR/stall.json, line STALL. 0 = off. The pass ceiling (--passes) and the time budget (--max-time) stay. Replay on the W10 OFF log (/tmp/w8/bb/A/run.log, 2026-10-11): routing was done at 167 s, the optimizer then spent 1535 s on a board with opens; stall_passes 2 would have stopped at pass 9 (36 open; the run reached 20 at pass 30, 11 after multi-start); W12 loop 0 with 2 stopped at pass 11 with 29 open, so the user set 5 (2026-10-11, the LLM-in-the-loop workflow: a stuck run is diagnosed, one upstream fix, retry, at most 3 loops per task).
